interface.title: LuxPlate Analyzer
interface.field: Microbiology / bioluminescent reporter assays (plate-reader kinetics, Varioskan OD600 + luminescence)
interface.stage_of_work: Raw data import, quality control, preprocessing (blank subtraction, cross-talk deconvolution, OD normalization), kinetic metric extraction, figures and simple statistics
interface.what_it_is_for: Takes raw Varioskan kinetic workbooks for lux-reporter strains through replicate matching, curve review, point and curve exclusion, and one-button blank/cross-talk/OD correction to kinetic metrics, figures and CSV/.luxplate exports.

data.note: Uploaded varioskan_SCFM2vsLB_Rep1.xlsx and Rep2.xlsx together in 'Un fichier contient tous les temps' mode. The app found 2 strains (PA14-lux, PAO1-lux), 2 media (LB, SCFM2), 36 curves and 12 blanks, 7 time points (0–6 h). The running app is one guided page in French with a 'Projet' sidebar. There was no separate Import tab and no prompt to pick the luminescence sheet, unlike the repo description. Downloads: analyse_multi_fichiers.luxplate (120 KB, binary), analyse_multi_fichiers_metriques_cinetiques.csv, analyse_multi_fichiers_donnees_finales.csv, croissance.svg, analyse_multi_fichiers_decisions_exclusion.csv.

tree.specific: Take Varioskan OD600/luminescence workbooks of PA14-lux and PAO1-lux in LB vs SCFM2 to blank- and cross-talk-corrected, OD-normalized luminescence, kinetic metrics, figures and exports

screens_never_reached: A separate 'Import' tab with explicit luminescence-sheet selection and download of the raw unaveraged long table: the running app shows only the 'Analyse guidée' single page, with no tabs or sheet prompt.
The 'Un fichier par temps' and 'Mode mixte' import flows after upload: the two test files each contain all time points, so I only selected these modes and never uploaded data in them.
'Diagnostic statistique' expander and populated p-values: with only 2 biological pairs the comparison table shows p = None.
Re-loaded project state from a .luxplate import: no .luxplate test file is available to upload.
not_done: Did not import a .luxplate project back into the app. Only the two .xlsx test files can be uploaded, so the round-trip of the saved state was not verified. The export did produce a 120 KB binary file.

Did not change the 'Paramètres de calcul' values (DO minimale, points per window, R²), the Affichage options (panel organisation, linear/log Y scales, 'Même axe Y', technical-replicate toggle) or the figure-size sliders, because of the action budget.
Did not add hypotheses manually or with the 'Toutes les souches : LB > SCFM2' generator. I only removed one from the stack.
Did not edit the replicate mapping or untick the cross-talk correction to compare against the uncorrected data.
Did not use the long table's own 'Download as CSV' toolbar button (the raw long-table download the repo description mentions), or the 'Toutes les figures (ZIP)', PNG or TIF downloads.
Did not look at the metric comparison figures (peak, peak time, AUC, doubling-time box plots, fold change vs P0) or use the strain filter in 'Courbes finales'.
Unexplained result: after the exclusions, 'Séries analysées' fell from 24 to 12 although only one sample curve (A10) was excluded. I did not open the Cinétique tab again to find out why.

The exported kinetic-metrics CSV has an empty lum_norm_auc_do_cutoff column even though the AUC cap of OD600 0.31 had been validated (screens/058.webp). I did not check whether the export ignores the cap or whether it was applied after the download.
The repo describes Figure Builder and statistics as not integrated, but the 'Courbes finales' tab did have working figure options, ordering, AUC capping and paired t-test/Holm comparisons.

open_fixes: A task and feature for the metric comparison figures (peak, peak time, AUC and doubling-time box plots, fold change vs P0) and the display controls (strain filter, 'Même axe Y', log/linear scales) need a new run, because no kept screen shows them being used.
Reloading a saved .luxplate project needs a run that has a .luxplate file to upload.
Inspecting and downloading the raw unaveraged long table needs a run that uses the table's CSV download.
Time-point matching in 'Un fichier par temps' / mixed mode needs test files that each hold a single time point.
Comparing results with and without cross-talk correction needs a run that unticks the correction and re-runs the analysis.
